# PROCESS — what I did this iteration (explainability; REQUIRED)

## Ranked issue list (clusters by # failing tasks × trials, biggest first)
Re-cluster ALL of the current champion's failures every round, not just last round's. agent-optimize's commit.py refuses a header-only table (--missing-ranked-issues-justification is the escape hatch).
| rank | cluster | tasks | shared root cause | tag (KNOWLEDGE / BEHAVIORAL / CAPABILITY-GAP) | planned change class |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | spec-epic authors real content a sibling content epic also authors (boundary overlap) | case-019 (reward 0.75, the only non-1.0 task) | Decomposer has no spec-vs-content boundary rule: E001 (packaging format) scope says "Produce a reference example of a correctly packaged tutorial" while E003 authors the six tutorials. Internal review (re-review) flagged it as minor; pipeline had already reached BATCH_DONE (review passed), so nothing fixed it. External scorer: "Epic Boundaries — solid with one minor overlap" → 4/5. | KNOWLEDGE (missing rule) + BEHAVIORAL (review catches it only stochastically — first review missed it, re-review found it) | missing-rule in decompose Step 5 + worked example; named pattern in review Criterion 3; must-fix class + correction recipe in revise; mechanical check in bundled script |
| 2 | docs-authoring epic priority not derived from strategy Jira priority | case-019 (E004 P2 vs Major→P1) | Rule exists in decompose Step 4 and review Criterion 1, but the decomposer copied HLR-4's P2 label instead; nothing enforces it deterministically. | BEHAVIORAL (rule known, skipped) | code enforcement: mechanical check in bundled script, run by decomposer (Step 8c), reviewer (Step 2.0), reviser (Step 4) |
| 3 | rollout gate named in scope with no matching AC | case-019 (E002 "feature flag / dashboard config gating" in scope, no gating AC) | Decompose Step 7 has no gating-coverage rule; review Criterion 6 doesn't name the pattern. | KNOWLEDGE (missing rule) | missing-rule in decompose Step 7; named pattern in review Criterion 6; must-fix class in revise; mechanical check in script |
| 4 | (latent, same mechanism as 1-3) structural contract breaches: unresolvable deps, branch files missing branch/gated_by, main-plan→branch deps, epic_count mismatch, missing ai-signals files, sibling draft-ID refs | no current val failures (defensive) | The review checks these by hand; the decomposer has no mechanical self-check. | CAPABILITY-GAP (no deterministic mechanism) | bundled script structural checks (same enforcement chain) |

Leverage: cluster 1 is the scored deduction (0.75→1.0 = +0.25 on 1/8 of val ≈ +0.031 reward); clusters 2-3 are the same review-passes-with-unfixed-minors mechanism and were also flagged in 019's final review.

## Changes made this iteration (one row per edit — aim for MULTIPLE classes, incl. a NEW tool when a cluster needs one)
| cluster | edit class | file / tool | what & why it generalizes | protects passing? |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | missing-rule + worked example | epic-decompose/prompts/decompose-agent.md (Step 5, Rule 2 new "Spec-vs-content boundary" axis bullet) | General boundary rule: a format/schema/standard-defining epic validates with a minimal stub, never authors real instances of a sibling authoring epic's deliverable; states both fix shapes (stub wording / subsume into authoring epic). Applies to any spec+content strategy, not just tutorials. | Yes — BOUNDED: fires only when a spec epic + content sibling coexist; verified absent from all 7 passing tasks (script scan of the same condition: 0 findings) |
| 3 | missing-rule | epic-decompose/prompts/decompose-agent.md (Step 7 "Gating coverage" bullet) | Any rollout gate named in scope (feature flag / config gate / toggle) needs a matching AC verifying gated behavior. | Yes — BOUNDED: condition unique to 019-E002 among val tasks (verified) |
| 1+2+3+4 | NEW bundled script (code enforcement) | epic-decompose/scripts/check_decomposition.py (new, 584 lines, real code, --self-check passes) | Mechanical checks for: docs-priority derivation, gating-AC gap, spec/content overlap, structural breaches (unresolvable deps, branch metadata, main→branch deps, epic_count, missing ai-signals files, sibling draft-ID refs). Each finding names file + defect + fix. Dependency-free (hand-rolled frontmatter parser). | Yes — BOUNDED: verified exit-0 on all 7 passing tasks' exact artifacts; flags exactly the 3 target findings on 019's artifacts |
| 1+2+3+4 | skipped-step → script invocation | epic-decompose/prompts/decompose-agent.md (Step 8c) | Decomposer must run the check and reach exit 0 before setting decompose_complete=true (the pipeline's finish sentinel). Robust path resolution for both runtime layouts (`skills/epic-decompose/*/scripts/…` + single-nested fallback). | Yes — on passing tasks the script exits 0 (one extra Bash call, "OK" output, no behavior change) |
| 1+2+3+4 | enriched review procedure (deterministic pre-check) | epic-decompose/prompts/review-agent.md (new Step 2.0) | Reviewer runs the same script first and folds findings into the issues list with per-class severity + criterion mapping. Makes the FIRST review catch what the 019 first review missed, so the unconditional first revision fixes it. | Yes — script exits 0 on passing tasks' post-decompose artifacts (verified; revision deltas of 014/017/018/020 don't intersect the check classes) |
| 1 | named pattern in rubric | epic-decompose/prompts/review-agent.md (Criterion 3 Check) | Names the spec-vs-content overlap pattern explicitly (with the reference-tutorial example) and its minor/major severity split — a strong-but-not-frontier reviewer needs the pattern named to catch it reliably. | Yes — pattern absent from all 7 passing tasks' artifacts |
| 3 | named pattern in rubric | epic-decompose/prompts/review-agent.md (Criterion 6 Check) | Gating-coverage check: gate named in scope without verifying AC = listed issue. | Yes — pattern absent from passing tasks |
| 1+2+3 | decision-rule narrowing (must-fix classes) | epic-decompose/prompts/revise-agent.md (Step 2) | Enumerates the defect classes that MUST be fixed even when marked minor (boundary overlap, gating-AC gap, docs-priority derivation, structural breaches); other minors (defensible-choice observations, arguable signal values) keep the agent's existing judgment latitude — verbatim preserves 015/016's leave-behavior and 017's fix-behavior. | Yes — verified per-task: 013 (no issues), 015/016 (observation minors → left, as now), 017 (signal fix → still allowed), 018/020 (major issues → still fixed) |
| 1 | correction recipe | epic-decompose/prompts/revise-agent.md (Epic Boundary issues list) | New "Spec-vs-content overlap" recipe: do NOT merge (the format/consumer boundary is correct) — restate as stub or subsume into the authoring epic. Prevents a wrong merge-style "fix". | Yes — new recipe only fires on the overlap class (absent from passing tasks) |
| 1+2+3+4 | verification step | epic-decompose/prompts/revise-agent.md (Step 4) | Reviser re-runs the script after corrections until exit 0, so a revision cannot leave a mechanically-detectable defect for the (terminal) re-review to find. | Yes — script exits 0 on passing tasks' post-revision artifacts (= final artifacts, verified) |

## Verify-the-fix (one line per change: the trace it targets → what the guard/computation/new-tool now does on those exact inputs)
- check_decomposition.py on case-019's exact artifacts (reconstructed from trajectory metadata.files): `FINDING [docs-priority] RHAISTRAT-9019-E004.md`, `FINDING [gating-ac] RHAISTRAT-9019-E002.md`, `FINDING [spec-content] RHAISTRAT-9019-E001.md`, exit 1 — exactly the three defects the internal re-review flagged and the scorer's "one minor overlap" names.
- check_decomposition.py on all 7 passing tasks' exact artifacts (case-013…case-020 excl. 019): exit 0, zero findings → the guard does NOT fire on any passing task (blast radius = 0).
- check_decomposition.py --self-check: 5 synthetic fixtures (clean, docs-priority, gating-ac, spec-content, structure) all produce the expected finding sets — ALL PASS.
- decompose-agent Step 5 rule vs 019 trace: E001's scope line "Produce a reference example of a correctly packaged tutorial" + E003 title "Author six curated tutorials…" is precisely the rule's trigger; both stated fix shapes eliminate the overlap the scorer docked.
- decompose-agent Step 7 rule vs 019 trace: E002 scope "feature flag / dashboard config gating for the gallery section" with no gating AC → rule requires the AC (or dropping the gate from scope).
- docs-priority derivation vs all 8 strategies: Critical(013,014)→P0 ✓, Major(015,018,019,020)→P1, Normal(016,017)→P2 — all 7 passing tasks' docs epics already match; only 019-E004 (P2, Major) deviates → guard fires only there.
- revise-agent Step 2 vs passing traces: 013 first review `issues=[]`; 015/016 observation minors ("defensible", "arguable") stay judgment-latitude; 017's signal-value fix stays judgment-latitude; 018 (critical DAG) / 020 (major gate metadata) unaffected (already must-fix by severity) — no passing task's revise behavior flips.
- script invocation path vs 019 runtime layout: observed skill location `skills/epic-decompose/epic-decompose/` matches the first glob; single-nested fallback covers the alternate layout.

## Process & features used
- Subagents / worktrees / parallel features used: none — serial. Rationale: only ONE non-passing task (case-019); the full cluster analysis fits in ~20 reads of one trace + programmatic scans of all 8 trajectories' artifacts. Subagent fan-out would have added turn overhead without coverage gain.
- Prior iterations I read from ./prior_iterations/ + ./RUNMAP.md: none exist (iteration 1; RUNMAP table empty, LEDGER has only the seed row, rejected.jsonl absent).

## Good things to PRESERVE (do not let a future iteration undo these)
- The bundled-script enforcement chain (decompose Step 8c → review Step 2.0 → revise Step 4) is one mechanism wired into three agents — keep them in sync if any leg is edited.
- The revise-agent's must-fix list is deliberately ENUMERATED (script defect classes only) so observation-minors keep their current leave/fix latitude — do not broaden it to "all minors" (would change 015/016/017/020 trajectories).
- The review-agent's pass/fail thresholds and the pipeline's cycle-cap semantics were deliberately NOT touched — only additive pattern-naming and a mechanical pre-check.

## Deliberately skipped (cluster + why — already-passing / needs gold / infra noise)
- **gate_failure_impact / gated_by completeness check in the script**: mechanically implementable (epic depending on an Investigation without gated_by, or gated_by without gate_failure_impact) but it fires on case-020's POST-DECOMPOSE state (its first review flagged exactly this as 3 majors; the revise agent fixed them). Adding it would change a passing task's trajectory (decomposer fixing at Step 8c instead of revise) — behavioral change on a passing task without verification that the decomposer's fix path lands identically. Candidate for a later iteration with that verification.
- **Making the review recommend `revise` whenever minors remain**: unbounded — 015/016/018/020 all pass with observation minors listed and score 5/5; forcing more revision cycles churns passing decompositions (regression risk via gratuitous edits) with no scored upside.
- **SKILL.md edits (description/trigger/body)**: the skill triggers and runs correctly on all 8 val tasks; the orchestrator prompt has no defect in this cluster. Editing the description risks trigger behavior for zero cluster coverage.
- **Fixing the truncated external-scorer feedback** (1288 chars, rationale cut mid-sentence): infra/framework issue, recorded in FRAMEWORK_IMPROVEMENTS.md, not editable here.
- **Jira attach/label steps not running** (no credentials in eval env): infra noise, not scored.

# DIAGNOSIS.json — machine-readable diagnosis (REQUIRED under agent-optimize)

Written to ./DIAGNOSIS.json (see file). Summary: 3 clusters (A: spec/content boundary overlap — the scored deduction; B: docs-priority derivation skipped; C: gating-AC gap), all on case-019, all enforced via one new bundled script + prompt rules wired into decompose/review/revise; 1 skipped cluster documented (gate metadata completeness — would touch passing case-020's trajectory).
